readings: areset is asynchronous: asserting areset immediately clears predict_history to 0, independent of clk (always @(posedge clk or posedge areset)).
areset is synchronous: predict_history clears to 0 only on the next posedge clk when areset is high, because all sequential logic is triggered on the positive edge of clk.
New history = {train_history[30:0], train_taken} (shift train_history left, insert train_taken at LSB, discard oldest bit train_history[31]).
New history = {train_history[31:1], train_taken} (discard train_history[0], so the branch immediately before the mispredicted branch is lost and the remaining bits are shifted right).

ambiguities.aspect: Priority between reset and other inputs
readings: Reset has highest priority: if areset=1, predict_history <= 0 regardless of predict_valid or train_mispredicted.
train_mispredicted (or predict_valid) takes priority over reset: if areset=1 and train_mispredicted=1, predict_history <= {train_history[30:0], train_taken}.
train_history uses the same convention as predict_history: bit 0 is the youngest branch.
train_history's bit ordering is unspecified or opposite: bit 31 is the youngest branch, which changes the concatenation order in the rollback load.
